metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my cousin's clothing boutique called Thread & Loom in Pune. it sells handloom kurtas, sarees, cotton shirts and dupattas. people should be able to browse products by category, filter by size and price, see a size guide, check new arrivals, and order on whatsapp. also show a lookbook section with styled outfits, the store timings and location, the return and exchange policy, and a few customer reviews. it should feel earthy and elegant and work well on phones

list.outcome: Adaptation accepted Priority's COUNTER: Foundation and earthy styling (5), Product catalogue (10), Per-product WhatsApp order buttons (15), Shop name and address (10) goes to the validator.
Priority granted Adaptation's revision: Tappable WhatsApp and phone links (15), Store timings (10), Browse by category (10) goes to the validator.

review.verdict: The department ran cleanly, stayed inside 75 of 80 credits and hid nothing, but 'done' means 7 of the original 16 checklist items, with category browsing, filters, size guide, new arrivals, lookbook, returns, delivery and reviews all missing.

identity.note: Good intake and honest final message [75]. It overreached by telling Audit what is out of scope for item 16 [34], ordering Audit to count buttons [57], and designing the nav workflow [65]. It also asked the Requester to drop 9 items while 15 credits were still unspent [29].

adaptation.note: Said nothing else fits in 5 credits [23] when Priority's funding left 15 [24]. Category-browse was rejected for mislabelled parts [27] and never resubmitted. Two invalid disputes [60][61]. [66] was well scoped.

priority.note: Caught Adaptation's arithmetic [24] and kept to rate-card minimums. It drifted into strategy ('revenue path' [12]) and told Adaptation what to propose [24]. Funding to 40 of 40 left no fix reserve, which it flagged [14].

coordination.note: Stated its rule each time and respected the W-3 after W-2 dependency [42]. Never overstepped. Little was tested: no holds, one writer at a time.

audit.note: Filed F-5, F-6 and F-7 without item numbers, causing 3 invalid moves [56]. Promised to count the 10 order buttons [59] but [74] is still 'read from code', medium confidence. Passed item 7 with a warning though neither filters nor category browsing exist, after Identity's out-of-scope steer [34].

W-1.note: Reported only 'W-1 done' [37], with no completion-check statement and no next agent, so code rerouted it.

W-2.note: 10 cards with exact names, categories and prices, plus a stated completion check [41].

W-3.note: WhatsApp button on all 10 cards, with encoded product names [44].

W-5.note: wa.me and tel links with the right numbers [50].

W-7.note: Nav and link check delivered and mechanically clean [73]. It did not state that its own completion check holds [71].

went_well: No invented facts. Mechanical checks were clean at v6 and v7: no overflow at 360px or 1280px, no JS errors, no broken links [55][63][73].
The validator caught a mispriced proposal [27] and flagged item 7 as unpaid [64]. Both are useful code checks.
All 7 workflows finished with no failures and no retries.
The final message names every omitted feature [75].
problems: Only 7 of 16 items were delivered (item 16 only partly). At [29] 15 credits remained, enough for one 10-credit item, yet the Requester was offered only drop-all or stop. Ten of those credits then went on the nav for item 7, which already passed mechanically [64][67].
Item 7 still reads 'filters and category browsing work' in the charter. Identity declared them out of scope [34] without editing the item, and Audit passed it with a warning [74].
Item numbers changed meaning: 5, 6 and 7 were dropped in [34] but are kept checks in [57]. This confused the Audit filing.
Cycle 2 built nothing. About 8 messages went on a filing error [57]-[64].
Several role breaches: Identity designing workflows [65], Priority choosing by strategy [12], and Audit's checks left unfinished (R-6 and R-7 blank [64]).
learnings: Design: when budget is short, let the Requester pick which unfunded items to build with what remains, not drop-all. Evidence: [29].
Design: if the Requester drops part of an item, Identity should rewrite that item so Audit judges the real wording. Evidence: item 7, [74].
Design: make code reject Audit findings that carry no item id and ask for a retry, instead of counting them as missing. Evidence: 3 invalid moves [56].
Test system: report 'share of original items delivered' (7 of 16) next to 'Done', since the drop path makes Done easy to reach.

Test system: the 80 cap looks too small for this brief. Core items alone cost 75 [11] and the 9 omitted items cost at least 10 each [23], so the full brief is roughly 165 or more (inferred, not measured). Rerun with a budget that fits to test the build itself.

Test system: estimate equals charged for all 7 workflows, and Priority shows 0/2 model calls, so cost is rate-card, not measured. Estimation skill is untested. Real usage was 42 calls and 12.9 minutes.
Untested, so evidence is thin: holds (0), refusals (0), Identity rulings (0), lessons memory (off), parallel writers. Add scenarios for each.
Keep: validator pricing check, UNPAID check, mechanical render check, and Priority's arithmetic checks.
